ordered_diagnoses: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the iris

s1.syndrome_frame: A vascularized iris mass with ciliary body involvement and anterior chamber angle involvement
salient_findings: 10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule
key_facts: Patient is a man in his late 60s
Presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
Slitlamp examination showed a vascularized iris nodule
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showed monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic lymphocytes
CD20+ lymphocytes were present
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation showed no other involvement
Staging was T2N0M0

raw.rationale: The presence of a vascularized iris nodule, ciliary body involvement, and monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic lymphocytes, specifically CD20+ lymphocytes, supports the diagnosis of iris lymphoma.

rejected.label: Uveal lymphoma
rejected.why: While uveal lymphoma could be considered, the specific involvement of the iris and the presence of CD20+ lymphocytes make iris lymphoma a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: MALT lymphoma of the iris
rejected.why: MALT lymphoma is a subtype of lymphoma, but the provided information does not specifically suggest MALT lymphoma characteristics.

rejected.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the iris
rejected.why: The lymphocytes described are small to medium-sized, which does not align with the typical large cell size seen in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Follicular lymphoma of the iris
rejected.why: There is no specific indication of follicular architecture or other characteristics typical of follicular lymphoma in the provided information.
